meta.titre: Atomic structure: particles, electron shells, ions and isotopes
meta.sous_theme: The atom and the Periodic Table

sections.contenu_markdown: Every object in a Douala market, from a plastic bucket to an iron bar, is built from atoms too small to see. Yet the way the electrons are arranged inside those atoms explains why sodium reacts violently with water, why neon never reacts at all, and why the salt on your plantain is harmless. The GCE O/L paper asks you to describe the atom, to work out numbers of particles, to write electronic configurations and to say whether an element is a metal. These questions are short and worth easy marks if you know the pattern.

items: All substances are made of atoms.
Protons are positive, electrons are negative and neutrons are neutral.
The Periodic Table lists elements by increasing atomic number.
A group is a vertical column of the Periodic Table and a period is a horizontal row.

sections.titre: The atom: particles, numbers, electron arrangement and isotopes
sections.contenu_markdown:
An atom has a tiny central **nucleus** made of **protons** and **neutrons**, and **electrons** that move in shells around it.

| Particle | Relative mass | Relative charge | Where found |
|---|---|---|---|
| Proton | 1 | +1 | Nucleus |
| Neutron | 1 | 0 | Nucleus |
| Electron | about $\frac{1}{1840}$ (negligible) | $-1$ | Shells around the nucleus |

An atom is **neutral**, so the number of electrons equals the number of protons.

The **atomic number** $Z$ is the number of protons. The **mass number** $A$ is the number of protons plus the number of neutrons, so the **number of neutrons = $A - Z$**. An atom of an element X is written ${}^{A}_{Z}\mathrm{X}$, for example ${}^{23}_{11}\mathrm{Na}$ has 11 protons, 11 electrons and 12 neutrons.

**Electron arrangement.** Electrons fill the shell nearest the nucleus first. The first shell holds a maximum of 2 electrons, the second holds 8 and the third holds 8 (for the first 20 elements). Sodium (11 electrons) is written **2,8,1**, chlorine (17) is **2,8,7**.

**The Periodic Table.** The number of **outer-shell electrons** is the **group number** (Group I has 1, Group VII has 7), and the number of **shells** is the **period number**. Sodium, 2,8,1, is in Group I and Period 3. A noble gas has a full outer shell and is unreactive.

**Metal or non-metal.** An atom with **1 to 3** outer electrons is usually a **metal**: it loses electrons to form a positive ion. An atom with **5 to 7** outer electrons is a **non-metal**: it gains electrons to form a negative ion.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When an atom gains or loses electrons
variantes.contenu_markdown:
An **ion** is a charged atom. Atoms gain or lose electrons to get a full outer shell, like a noble gas. The number of protons does not change.

| Atom | Change | Ion | Electrons in the ion |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sodium, 2,8,1 | loses 1 electron | $\mathrm{Na^{+}}$ | 2,8 |
| Magnesium, 2,8,2 | loses 2 electrons | $\mathrm{Mg^{2+}}$ | 2,8 |
| Chlorine, 2,8,7 | gains 1 electron | $\mathrm{Cl^{-}}$ | 2,8,8 |
| Oxygen, 2,6 | gains 2 electrons | $\mathrm{O^{2-}}$ | 2,8 |

variantes.quand_utiliser: When atoms of the same element have different mass numbers
variantes.contenu_markdown:
**Isotopes** are atoms of the same element with the **same atomic number** but **different mass numbers**, because they have different numbers of neutrons. Isotopes have the same chemical properties because they have the same number of electrons.

Chlorine has two isotopes: ${}^{35}\mathrm{Cl}$ (18 neutrons) and ${}^{37}\mathrm{Cl}$ (20 neutrons). In a sample, about 75% of the atoms are chlorine-35 and 25% are chlorine-37.

The **relative atomic mass** is the average mass of the isotopes, taking their percentages into account:

$A_r = \dfrac{(75 \times 35) + (25 \times 37)}{100} = 35.5$

Some isotopes are radioactive. Examples of their use include carbon-14 for dating old objects and cobalt-60 for treating cancer.

sections.enonce_markdown: An atom of element **E** has atomic number 20 and mass number 40. (a) State the number of protons, neutrons and electrons. (b) Write its electronic configuration. (c) State its group and period and say whether it is a metal. (d) Give the formula of the ion it forms and the electron arrangement of that ion.

etapes.justification: The atomic number equals the number of protons, and a neutral atom has the same number of electrons.
Fill 2 in the first shell, then 8, then 8, and the rest in the fourth.

etapes.action: State the group, period and type.
etapes.justification: Outer electrons give the group; the number of shells gives the period.
etapes.resultat_markdown: 2 outer electrons: **Group II**; 4 shells: **Period 4**. With 2 outer electrons, E is a **metal** (calcium).

etapes.justification: A metal atom loses its outer electrons to reach a full shell.
etapes.resultat_markdown: E loses 2 electrons: $\mathrm{Ca^{2+}}$, with 18 electrons arranged **2,8,8**

sections.conclusion_markdown: E has **20 protons, 20 neutrons and 20 electrons**, configuration **2,8,8,2**; it is a metal in **Group II, Period 4**, and forms **$\mathrm{Ca^{2+}}$**.

items.erreur_markdown: The mass number is the number of protons.
items.pourquoi_faux: The number of protons is the atomic number. The mass number counts the protons and neutrons together.
items.correction_markdown: Mass number $A$ = protons + neutrons, so neutrons = $A - Z$.

items.erreur_markdown: Electrons are in the nucleus and are as heavy as protons.
items.pourquoi_faux: Electrons move in shells around the nucleus. Their mass is negligible compared with a proton.
items.correction_markdown: The nucleus holds protons and neutrons only.

items.erreur_markdown: Isotopes of an element have different numbers of protons.
items.pourquoi_faux: A different number of protons means a different element. Isotopes differ in neutrons.
items.correction_markdown: Isotopes have the **same atomic number** and **different mass numbers**.

items.erreur_markdown: The configuration of sodium (11 electrons) is 2,9.
items.pourquoi_faux: The second shell holds a maximum of 8 electrons.

items.erreur_markdown: A sulphur atom, 2,8,6, loses 6 electrons to form $\mathrm{S^{6+}}$.
items.pourquoi_faux: Atoms with 5 to 7 outer electrons gain electrons to complete the shell, because that needs fewer electrons.

items.enonce_markdown: An atom of phosphorus has atomic number 15 and mass number 31. State (a) the numbers of protons, neutrons and electrons, (b) its electronic configuration, and (c) its group and period, and whether it is a metal or a non-metal.
items.solution_markdown: (a) Protons **15**, electrons **15**, neutrons $31 - 15 = $ **16**. (b) **2,8,5**. (c) 5 outer electrons: **Group V**; 3 shells: **Period 3**; it is a **non-metal** because it has 5 outer electrons and gains electrons.

items.enonce_markdown: Boron has two isotopes: ${}^{10}\mathrm{B}$ (20% of atoms) and ${}^{11}\mathrm{B}$ (80% of atoms). (a) State the number of neutrons in each isotope (boron has atomic number 5). (b) Calculate the relative atomic mass of boron. (c) Say why the two isotopes react in the same way.
items.solution_markdown: (a) ${}^{10}\mathrm{B}$: $10 - 5 = $ **5** neutrons; ${}^{11}\mathrm{B}$: $11 - 5 = $ **6** neutrons. (b) $A_r = \dfrac{(20 \times 10) + (80 \times 11)}{100} = \dfrac{200 + 880}{100} = $ **10.8**. (c) They have the **same number of electrons** (5), so they have the same electron arrangement and the same chemical properties.

items.enonce_markdown: An ion $\mathrm{Y^{2-}}$ has 18 electrons and 16 neutrons. (a) How many protons does Y have? (b) Calculate its mass number. (c) Write the electronic configuration of the Y atom and of the $\mathrm{Y^{2-}}$ ion. (d) Say whether Y is a metal and explain how the ion forms.
items.solution_markdown: (a) The ion has gained 2 electrons, so the atom has $18 - 2 = $ **16 electrons**, and so **16 protons**. (b) $16 + 16 = $ **32**. (c) Atom: **2,8,6**. Ion: **2,8,8**. (d) Y is a **non-metal** (sulphur), because it has 6 outer electrons. It **gains 2 electrons** to complete its outer shell and becomes $\mathrm{Y^{2-}}$.

items_markdown: Protons (+1) and neutrons (0) are in the nucleus; electrons ($-1$, negligible mass) are in shells.
Atomic number = protons = electrons; mass number = protons + neutrons; neutrons $= A - Z$.
Shells hold 2, 8, 8 electrons: outer electrons give the group, shells give the period.
Metals have 1 to 3 outer electrons and lose them; non-metals have 5 to 7 and gain electrons.
Isotopes have the same $Z$ but different $A$; $A_r$ is the weighted average of the isotope masses.
